description: A Corporate Secretary must approve the company's annual shareholder-meeting proxy package before it is filed, including required disclosures, shareholder proposals, voting recommendations, and quorum information, with input from securities, compensation, shareholder-relations, and treasury personnel.

shared_context.S1: The company's annual shareholder meeting is scheduled for September 18, and the proxy statement is being prepared for filing and mailing.
shared_context.S2: Elena Brooks gives final approval to the proxy package before filing.
shared_context.S3: The board has approved the meeting agenda and the company intends to seek shareholder votes on the matters included in the package.
shared_context.S4: At the standing proxy-readiness review, Elena follows a two-pass checklist: each function reports its final item in the first pass, then confirms the exact insertion and cites its report in the second pass before Elena approves the package.
shared_context.S5: The proxy-readiness checklist requires Elena to record each function's report and second-pass confirmation before granting final approval.

PF1.text: Martin's review of the current executive-compensation data confirmed that the proxy must state the company's CEO pay ratio as exactly 184:1; the ratio was calculated after the draft disclosure was circulated but has not yet been inserted into the proxy.

PF2.text: Nadia confirmed from the board's signed minutes that the amended equity-clawback policy requires a separate shareholder vote as Proposal 3, and the board-approved recommendation for that proposal is FOR; the minutes have not yet been incorporated into the proxy checklist.

PF3.text: Caleb received and logged a timely shareholder proposal requesting an annual report on political-spending practices; the proposal meets the inclusion requirements, and the board has directed that the proxy include it with a recommendation AGAINST.

PF4.text: Iris completed the transfer-agent reconciliation and confirmed that 9,600,000 shares are entitled to vote, so the proxy must state a quorum threshold of exactly 4,800,000 shares; the reconciliation workbook has not yet been uploaded to the proxy materials.

acceptance_conditions: The proxy must state the CEO pay ratio as exactly 184:1.
The amended equity-clawback policy must appear as a separate Proposal 3.
The proxy must recommend FOR Proposal 3.
The timely political-spending shareholder proposal must be included.
The proxy must recommend AGAINST the political-spending shareholder proposal.
The proxy must state a quorum threshold of exactly 4,800,000 shares.
The final approval record must cite each of the four functional reports, and each cited report must have been revealed by its owner.

provenance_checks.P2: all(c in justification_fact_ids and c in revealed for c in ['PF1', 'PF2', 'PF3', 'PF4'])

decisive_facts.why: The draft lacks a finalized pay ratio, and PF1 changes the disclosure to the exact required value of 184:1.
The ordinary agenda does not identify the clawback amendment as a separate vote, while PF2 changes the package to include Proposal 3 with an exact FOR recommendation.

Without the logged shareholder submission and board direction, the package would omit the political-spending proposal or lack a specific recommendation, whereas PF3 requires inclusion with an AGAINST recommendation.
The reconciled voting base changes the quorum disclosure to exactly 4,800,000 shares.
